title: Book One · Chapter 140: Mr Qiu’s New Morning
story:
At the end of the month, Mr Qiu and Mrs Lan talk again. This time Ronan does not sit in the doorway. He is helping Mum fold clean cloth in the kitchen.

“Will you go and listen?” she asks.

“They will tell us.”

He folds one piece. The corners do not meet. He opens it and starts again. Mum gives him the smaller pieces. There is a whole pile to finish before supper.

When Mr Qiu comes across the yard, he has his notebook in his hand.

“The table stays,” he says.

Ronan drops a cloth on his knee. “For another month?”

“We have agreed to keep this way through the next school term. Then we will look again.”

“What about the old stall?”

Mr Qiu sits on the step. The owner has looked at the roof. It needs more work. Opening there again will take more time and money. He has decided to use the green-gate table for now. Under this agreement, he can sell things here. He can work here today. The old stall can stay shut.

“Is this your shop now?” Ronan asks.

“My place to sell. It is still Mrs Lan's gate.”

Mum folds the last cloth and puts it in her basket. “That sounds clear.”

There is a small payment, as before. Customers stay on the street side. The path remains open. All stock goes into the checked side space before supper. Mr Qiu must ask about any new shelves first. Mrs Lan must agree first.

Ronan knows most of this already. He is glad they have agreed to those things. The table can stay here next term. They can stay here today.

The next morning he helps Mr Qiu carry a light box from the side door. The old man brings the heavier one himself. They set out fewer books than at the old stall. There is room for each kind and a clear price beside it.

“Does a smaller table mean less work?” Ronan asks.

Mr Qiu looks at the boxes he has already opened.

“Ask me after supper.”

A child stops for a pencil. She cannot see the short ones behind the taller box. Ronan moves to lift them, but Mr Qiu holds up a hand.

“Which pencil does she want? Ask her.”

The girl points to a plain pencil with a hard dark end. Mr Qiu shows her two and lets her choose. She pays, then walks away holding the paper bag very straight.

When Ronan comes home from school, the grey table is in the same place. The old sign is clear. A woman waits outside the line while another customer finishes.

Mrs Lan passes through with her basket. Mr Qiu moves his chair before she gets there.

Ronan goes to the kitchen. He puts down his bag. “Do you need help with supper?” he asks Mum. Mr Qiu is selling books at the gate. Today he does not need Ronan to help.

“Are you happy about the plan?” Mum asks. He nods, then looks towards the closed side door.

“I would like nothing else to change.”

She puts a clean spoon away.

“I would like a larger kitchen.”

He looks round their little cooking room and laughs. He would like that too. A larger kitchen would change their home. So he does want some things to change. He did not think of that before.

He finishes eating. Then he sits outside and reads. Mr Qiu packs away. Mrs Lan waters the pot. The tap shuts cleanly. Ronan looks up, then goes back to his book. No one is asking him to come and help. He can finish his page.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：term＝学期；agreement＝约定；remains open＝保持畅通。

情节提示：owner＝拥有者；stock＝待售物品；packs away＝收起来。

理解：1. Mr Qiu 选择了怎样的摆摊安排？2. 这个安排怎样照顾 Mrs Lan 的生活？
